answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.THANKSGIVING: In the United States, Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday of November. Families differ in their meals and activities.

answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.PIECE: A piece is one part of a whole. Matching shape, color, and edges helps a jigsaw piece fit its correct place.
answerNotes.THANKSGIVING: In the United States, Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday of November. Families differ in their meals and activities.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.FORK: A fork's prongs hold pieces of food. A garden fork is a larger tool sharing that pronged shape.

answerNotes.CORNUCOPIA: Cornucopia means a horn-shaped container overflowing with produce. It is a harvest decoration rather than a particular kind of fruit.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.APPLE: An apple has a peel, flesh, and a seed-bearing core. Cider is made by pressing apples for their juice.
answerNotes.NUT: In cooking, nut names foods such as almonds and walnuts. Botanical classifications are more detailed than this everyday food category.
answerNotes.THANKSGIVING: In the United States, Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday of November. Families differ in their meals and activities.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.

answerNotes.FOOTBALL: American football uses an oval ball and teams playing toward end zones. The puzzle concerns equipment and watching, not detailed rule recall.
answerNotes.TEAM: A team is a group playing together. In a home-and-away matchup, the home side plays at its own usual venue.
answerNotes.BALL: A ball is usually round in games such as baseball. American football uses a different, elongated shape.
answerNotes.PASS: A pass sends the football to another player. In an entryway or theater, the same word can instead mean permission to enter.
answerNotes.SCORE: A score records points earned. It is different from the game clock, which shows time remaining.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.THANKSGIVING: In the United States, Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday of November. Families differ in their meals and activities.
answerNotes.GAME: Game names the organized activity or contest. Equipment such as a bat or board is used in the game but is not the game itself.
answerNotes.WATCH: Watch can be a wrist timepiece or the action of looking attentively. A football-viewing scene uses the action rather than the object.

answerNotes.CRUST: Crust can mean a pie's pastry shell or a loaf's baked outer surface. Both are outer parts, but they are made differently.
answerNotes.CREAM: Cream is the rich part of milk. Whipping adds air, which is why whipped cream becomes fluffy.
answerNotes.CHEESE: Cheese comes in many textures and flavors. Sharp describes flavor, while a wedge describes the shape of a cut portion.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.PAN: Pan is a broad kitchen word. A frying pan is used on a stove, while a loaf pan holds dough or batter in the oven.
answerNotes.CINNAMON: Cinnamon comes from bark. It is sold in rolled sticks as well as ground into a fine powder.
answerNotes.THANKSGIVING: In the United States, Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday of November. Families differ in their meals and activities.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
